answer: Each identity runs one sparrow passage post and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files a quill-signed tally of violet-banded sparrow passage, with serials in a public log. An auditor recomputes it from the violet band table and post log; a duplicate serial, reused tally, or mismatch burns the bond. The first filing costs 34 credits; the kth fake pays 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6028 and 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 80,000 locked, with no sharing. A rented-post ring fails: each violet serial binds to one post key. An honest keeper pays 34 once, reclaims the bond after a clean audit.
